research_question: In adults with active systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), what is the effect of belimumab at standard approved doses (10 mg/kg IV or 200 mg SC) compared with placebo on achieving at least a 4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI score at 52 weeks?
treatment_label: Belimumab (10 mg/kg IV or 200 mg SC)
outcome_description: Dichotomous rate of participants achieving at least a 4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI score from baseline to 52 weeks
positive_direction: A risk ratio greater than 1.0 indicates a higher probability of achieving a ≥4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI at 52 weeks, favoring belimumab over placebo.
search_queries: belimumab systemic lupus erythematosus randomized controlled trial SELENA-SLEDAI
belimumab placebo active SLE trial 52 weeks outcome
belimumab lupus randomized trial SELENA-SLEDAI 4-point reduction
inclusion_criteria: Randomized controlled trials of adult patients diagnosed with active systemic lupus erythematosus
Trials comparing belimumab at standard approved dosing (10 mg/kg IV or 200 mg SC) with placebo
Studies reporting quantitative outcome data on achieving at least a 4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI score at 52 weeks
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, and commentaries are excluded)
Non-randomized studies or studies lacking a placebo control arm
Studies with no quantitative dichotomous data for the ≥4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI at 52 weeks
Studies evaluating only non-approved belimumab dosing regimens without a standard 10 mg/kg IV or 200 mg SC arm
moderators_to_extract: Route of administration (intravenous 10 mg/kg vs. subcutaneous 200 mg)
Baseline mean SELENA-SLEDAI disease activity score
Concomitant background immunosuppressant and corticosteroid regimens
Geographic region or predominant patient racial/ethnic distribution
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) is defined as the incidence rate of achieving a ≥4-point reduction in SELENA-SLEDAI at 52 weeks in the belimumab group divided by that in the placebo group. Only the approved 10 mg/kg IV or 200 mg SC weekly dose arms are compared against placebo.
